sara: quick heads-up — canary p99 jumped to ~1.8s at 03:12 UTC. correlates with a small set of requests that have very long prompts + tool-calls. I pasted a tiny profiler snapshot below, can anyone triage?

mike: on it. do we have a sample request id?

sara: req=canary_3a7bf, user prompt ~12k chars, calls to external tool that returns json w/ long arrays. KV cache shows a bunch of evictions around the same time.

lee: interesting — my quick grep of traces shows repeated kernel handoffs on that session: kernel_switch_count=9. that smells like repeated kernel selection between sparse and dense paths.

anya: could tool-call serialization be blowing up tokenization and causing microbatch to inflate? i saw avg_batch spike to 4 for that pod. :thinking_face:

sara: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
timeline: [recv->tokenize->kv-lookup->kernelA->kernelB->kv-evict->kernelA->emit]
kernel_switch_count=9
kv_cache_evictions=28
avg_batch_size=3.9
p95=480ms p99=1.82s
long_prompt_tokens=9200
tool_call_latency=210ms (per call), tool_calls=3
prefix_cache_hits=0\n```

jonas: that "kernelA->kernelB->kernelA" loop is the killer. we recompile kernelB for long-seq path which invalidates some optimized kernels and causes fallback; compile + warmup costs are non-trivial.

mike: confirm — kernel selection heuristic is seeing mixed sequence-length signals (part of prompt small, then long tool output), so it oscillates. I can reproduce locally with a script.

lee: reproducer would be great. if it's deterministic, we can add a guard to prefer stable kernel once session length crosses threshold.

anya: also KV cache eviction pattern: tool outputs have many unique prefixes, so prefix/KV entries exhaust bucket and we evict active entries, forcing repeated kv-fill on subsequent tokens -> I/O spikes. we should check bucket sizes and admission policy.

mike: quick experiment results: toggling `prefer_stable_kernel=true` on one canary pod drops kernel_switch_count to 1 and p99 to 540ms, but throughput drops ~6%. tradeoff visible.

deploy-bot: deploy start: canary toggle prefer_stable_kernel on pod canary-7f (user=infra)

jonas: that matches the expected SLO vs throughput tradeoff — stable kernel reduces compile/warmup and avoids oscillation but we pay in per-token efficiency for some shorter sequences.

sara: proposed steps: 1) roll a canary with stable-kernel guard for sessions > 2k tokens 2) bump KV admission size on canaries to reduce eviction churn 3) add a rule: if tool_call_count>=2 in last 5s, bias selection to long-seq kernel to avoid flip-flop.

lee: +1. also add lightweight tracing to record kernel_switch_count per session so we can alert on >3 switches within 30s.

anya: I'll prototype KV admission bump (from 512 -> 2048 entries) and run mem/latency smoke. canary runs on me.

mike: I'll push the kernel bias toggle and test with reproducer. will post results.

jonas: FYI long-term we should consider kernel warmstart snapshots for compiled kernels so fallback cost is low. adding to roadmap.

deploy-bot: deploy success: canary toggle prefer_stable_kernel on pod canary-7f (duration 00:00:12)

mike: quick numbers after toggles on 3 canaries: p99 down from 1.82s -> 610ms, p95 steady, throughput -5.8%. KV eviction rate down ~70%.

sara: nice. let's keep the canary for 24h and run traffic-weighted experiments (20% baseline, 80% guarded) to measure user-visible regressions. if stable after 24h, we'll promote and open a follow-up to refine kernel heuristics.

lee: adding alert rule to detect kernel_switch_count > 3 per session. will also surface sessions with repeated tool_call loops.

anya: started canary run, will post mem/eviction graphs in #eng-runtime after 1h. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sara: thanks everyone — good triage. filing short postmortem if the canary confirms root cause (kernel flip + kv churn triggered by long prompts + tool-call expansion).

mike: one last note: reproducer script lives at `tools/repro/longprompt-toolloop.sh` (small harness, uses local model weights). ping me if you need access.

jonas: excellent. follow-ups: (a) short-term guard rollout (b) KV admission tweak (c) longer-term kernel warmstart snapshots + smarter kernel bias ML model.

sara: closing loop here for now. leave comments if you want to be on the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
